claim: lock_coordination_example: `LOCKTRY lock_id WC        ' Try to acquire lock` / `IF_C  JMP #try_again      ' C=1 means locked by other COG`. LOCKTRY sets C=1 when the lock WAS taken (C=0: held by another cog or not allocated), so the retry branch is inverted -- the cog that got the lock jumps back and tries again, and a cog that did not get it goes on to drive the pin. The correct test is `IF_NC JMP #try_again`. multi_cog_synchronization.yaml:30 and :33-34 on the same subject state it correctly (`C=1 if acquired`; `if_nc ret ' Failed`). The block compiles, so the gate cannot see it.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:270 (LOCKTRY: `C = 1 if got LOCK`); engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:3688

claim: ALTB examples do not address what the comments say. `ALTB bit_num, #0` then `BITH flags, #0-0 ' Actually sets bit 7` (and bit_scan `ALTB bit_pos` + `TESTB flags, #0-0 WC`): ALTB replaces the next instruction's D field (the register) with (D[13:5] + S) & $1FF and leaves S alone, so the target register becomes register 0 (bit_num[13:5]=0, S=0) -- `flags` is never touched -- and the bit number stays the literal `#0-0` = 0. The silicon-doc form is `ALTB bitindex,#base` then `BITC 0,bitindex` (D placeholder, S = the register holding the bit index). The page's own description (:73-75 'Next instruction's bit field = base + bit_reg[4:0]') is the same misreading. All of it compiles.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:546-560 (`ALTB bitindex,#base` / `BITC 0,bitindex`; `ALTB bitindex` / `TESTB 0,bitindex WC`); engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:144-145

claim: `MOV offset, #3` / `ALTR offset, #0` / `ADD base_reg, value ' Result goes to base_reg+3`: ALTR sets the result register to (D + S) & $1FF = 3 + 0 = register 3, not base_reg+3 (the base must be the S operand: `ALTR offset, #base_reg`), and the ADD's own D (`base_reg`) is then only the operand read. Same family: addressing_modes.yaml:110 `ALTR index ' Next result = cog[D + index]` (the one-operand form sets the result register to D[8:0], i.e. cog[index]).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:529 (`ALTR index,#table` sets next write to table+index), :542; engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:138-139

claim: attention_handler: `SETINT3 #12      ' ATN event`. Event 12 is 'streamer NCO rollover'; attention (ATN) is event 14 -- the same page's own table (:104, :106) says so. As written the ISR fires on streamer rollovers and never on COGATN.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:2051, :2053 (Event 12 = Streamer NCO rollover; Event 14 = Attention)

claim: RESIx described as 'Resume from interrupt (continue interrupted code) / Like RETI but continues interrupted instruction'. RESIx = `CALLD IJMPx,IRETx WCZ`: it returns to the interrupted program but records the ISR's next address in IJMPx, so the NEXT interrupt resumes the ISR after the RESI (a co-routine style ISR); RETIx restarts at IJMPx each time.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:2313-2317

claim: CALLA/CALLB: 'operation: PTRx = PC + 4, then jump' / 'Return address in PTRA' / 'Save return in PTRA, not stack'. CALLA writes {C, Z, 10'b0, PC[19:0]} to the hub long at PTRA++ (CALLB: PTRB++), i.e. it PUSHES onto a hub stack addressed by PTRA, and RETA/RETB pop it. PTRA is not set to the return address; PTRA is advanced by 4 per call and the hub write costs 5...12 (cog) / 14...32 clocks, so 'no stack needed' / 'leaf functions' (:72, :198) is also off -- it needs a stack in hub RAM.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:344, :346, :428-429 (CALLA/CALLB write to hub long at PTRA++/PTRB++)

claim: `GETPTR reg ' Read PTRA/PTRB value` and 'explicit via GETPTR/SETPTR'. GETPTR returns the current hub FIFO pointer (D = FIFO hub address), not PTRA/PTRB (those are ordinary registers $1F8/$1F9: `MOV x, PTRA`). There is no SETPTR instruction (0 hits in the instruction table).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:352 (`GETPTR D ... Get current FIFO hub pointer into D`); engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:5336, :1174

claim: special_registers.yaml:54 `features: True random based on thermal noise` (GETRND is the xoroshiro128** PRNG; registered S-023); :84 `Q receives quotient from DIV operations` and :43 'Quotient/auxiliary register': P2 has no DIV instruction, SETQ sets Q for the NEXT block/CORDIC instruction, and CORDIC results come from GETQX/GETQY (QDIV quotient in X).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:337 (SETQ: `Set Q to D`); S-023 rows in the study

claim: non_blocking_check: `POLLQMT WC ' C=1 if pipeline empty` / `IF_NC GETQX result ' Retrieve only if available`. The QMT event flag is set when a GETQX/GETQY ALREADY executed with no result queued or in progress (event 15), and POLLQMT reads-and-clears that history bit; it says nothing about a result still being computed, and a GETQX issued while a result is in flight simply waits for it. The page states the event correctly itself at :155-157. There is no non-blocking 'result ready' poll for the CORDIC.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:2054, :2207-2211, :3413

claim: REP block-size operands that do not match the body: bit_reversal `REP #32, #32` over a 2-instruction body (it repeats the next 32 instructions); multiply_accumulate `REP #2, #16` over THREE instructions (RDLONG/MUL/ADD); register_indirection increment_modes `REP #4, #10` and array_copy `REP #2, count` over three instructions each. `conditional_rep`: `IF_NZ REP #4, count ' Loop body executes only if count > 0` -- when the REP is skipped (count = 0) the four body instructions still run once as ordinary code (and a REP executed with S = 0 repeats forever). The blocks compile, the gate cannot see the mismatch.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:257 (`REP`: next D[8:0] instructions S times; S = 0 repeats infinitely); engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:757-759

claim: rep_instruction.yaml:15 gives block_size '0-511 with #, 0-2^32-1 with ## or register' and :22 'block_size: Extended via AUGD prefix (0 to 2^32-1)', yet :66 says 'Maximum 511 instructions per block (9-bit D field)' -- only D[8:0] is used (0..511). :67 'Maximum 512 iterations (immediate)': a `#` immediate is 0..511, and the count is S[31:0]. :94 lists JMP/CALL/RET as not allowed in a REP block while :202 teaches `IF_Z JMP #found ' Exits REP block` and the silicon doc says any branch inside simply cancels REP.

claim: DJNF: 'loop body runs max(1, count) times; SAFE for count=0'. DJNF decrements and jumps while the result is not $FFFF_FFFF, so the body runs count+1 times (count = 0 once, count = 3 four times). The zero-start remark (:58-60) is right; the general formula is not.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:195 (`DJNF D,{#}S` ... jump if result is not $FFFF_FFFF)

claim: `bits_per_streamer_clk = 2^32 / SETXFRQ_value`: the NCO fraction is SETXFRQ_value / $8000_0000 (full scale $8000_0000, not 2^32) and it is the fraction of sysclk, not 'bits per streamer clock' of the inverse. With the page's own numbers the formula gives 2^32/$4000_0000 = 4 where the text says 1 bit per 2 sysclks. The worked values ($4000_0000 = sysclk/2, $2000_0000 = sysclk/4) are right.

claim: `rdlong value, hub_ptr  wc ' Read from hub, set C if non-zero` -- RDLONG WC puts the MSB (bit 31) of the long in C, not 'non-zero' (WZ gives zero); and `waitx ##20-2 ' Wait for hub window` -- WAITX only burns clocks, the hub access aligns itself to the egg-beater slot (9...16 clocks); there is no hub-window wait to code. The pattern ('hub synchronization') therefore synchronizes nothing.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:178 (`RDLONG ... C = MSB of long`)

Also `branchless_min_max` (:224) uses unsigned CMP (`IF_C MOV min_val, a`), fine for unsigned only.
